newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close firmer, Philips at new high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close firmer, Philips at new high.

text.p: Dutch shares were pushed higher at the close on Tuesday as Wall Street began to rise after a hesitant start.
Dealers said a firmer dollar and bond market had also boosted sentiment.
The main AEX share index rose 4.51 points to 811.99 and the AMX index for medium sized stocks added 7.75 points to 1281.03.

Philips climbed to a new high of 113.70 guilders, up 3.70 guilders. "The stronger dollar supported Philips," said one dealer, adding he could not find another reason for the strong increase in the share price.
Bourse newcomer Nutreco topped the volume list, closing 5.00 guilders up at 42.00 guilders, after being floated at 37.00.
"The rise of the stock shows that the climate for new issues is very favourable in Amsterdam, which is good for other stocks that will follow in the near term," said one dealer.
Vedior, the temporary employment arm of retail and business services group Vendex, will be floated at a price of 33 to 37 guilders per share on June 5.
Vendex closed at a new high of 112.00 guilders today, up 3.20 guilders from Monday's close.
Another dealer said several investors were unhappy with the allocation of Nutreco.
"One of my clients had subscribed for 900,000 Nutreco shares and received 1,000. He gave them back," the dealer said.
Before trading began in the shares it was already clear that the issue was heavily oversubscribed.
Most dealers remained upbeat about the market as a whole, though there were some doubts as the quarrel in Germany on the revaluation of the country's gold reserves continued.
"One of them has to go: (Bundesbank president) Tietmeyer or (Finance Minister) Waigel," said one dealer.
Several dealers fear for the future of economic and monetary union (EMU) as result of the quarrel in Germany.
They also said the new government in France still had to indicate its stance on the EMU.
"If the outlook for EMU remains uncertain this could trigger a slight correction in the share market," said one dealer.
"Beside this, an AEX index between 780-790 points looks more healthy anyway then the current level," he added.
Post and telecoms group KPN was up all day on a newspaper report in which analysts suggested KPN should be split in two.
